implementation_state: The whole substrate exists and is reachable from production code. AppState owns an AccountStore behind the optional account feature; ProviderConfig::accounts is the declaration; account::reconcile probes through a dyn shim and publishes into the store including on failure; and AppState::reconcile_accounts is the caller that was missing, which reads the currently loaded configuration, resolves each account's own credential reference through the real SecretStore, builds one adapter per account, and never returns without publishing a runtime for every declared enabled account. The two reasons this node was PARTIAL — that no call site invoked the reconciler and that no credential-resolution path fed it — are both now false. Two decisions inside the caller are recorded rather than left implicit: a missing backend and a backend that refused to build are kept distinct, because collapsing them makes a misconfigured panel indistinguishable from a feature-gated build; and one adapter is built per account rather than per provider, because an adapter holds exactly one credential and two accounts sharing a provider credential would otherwise be probed with each other's key. Check-in is the second account-owned execution surface and the only one that can run without a person: the maintenance block on AccountConfig — checkin_enabled, checkin_interval_secs, checkin_path and checkin_trigger_selector — is consumed by account::checkin::decide, a pure function of the declaration, the last settlement and an injected instant, and a minute timer in the desktop shell walks the declared accounts and starts the ones it calls Due. The settlement history that decision reads is durable, because the in-memory view a panel renders is empty on every launch and reading a schedule from it would make every account look untried after every restart. The scheduler deliberately does not guess: an account with no recorded settlement is refused as NeedsFirstObservation even when an interval is declared, because nothing is known about when a given relay's daily reset falls and opening one browser per account at launch is the failure being guarded against, so automation begins only after a person has started one check-in per account. A provider-neutral observation layer (ObservedResourceEvent, ResourceEffect, ObservedProviderAccounting) records what a finished check-in actually did into a bounded AccountEventLog and carries it to the snapshot through a bounded projection, so an observed event reaches something that reads it. What is NOT claimed here is a product surface for the reconciler: the account feature exposes a desktop command that reaches reconcile_accounts, and that gap belonged to UI-NEW-TRACKS and its Real surfaces gate rather than to this node's three gates. UI-NEW-TRACKS has since closed, and the account page now drives the reconciler through the refresh that also updates provider-level balances, so the gap this paragraph described is closed rather than carried. Two limits are stated rather than hidden: the event log is in memory, so its contents do not survive a restart, and the reconciler runs on the same manual refresh that updates provider-level balances rather than on a timer of its own, because there is no balance timer in this application and one account is one provider API call that nobody asked to repeat every minute. See E-119, E-120, E-130, E-131, E-132, E-134.
required_gates: Generic account types and pure calculations
unblock_condition: Revalidate Stage 5 and add an owned persistence/runtime contract without changing ML feature order.
notes: Check-in is the second account-owned execution surface and the only one that can now run without a person, behind an opt-in feature. The reconciler is called by the manual refresh command and its credential path resolves per account, so both of the things that used to be missing are present. The observation layer is no longer a type without a consumer: a confirmed check-in reaches the account event log and the snapshot. The event log is in memory and bounded, so it explains a balance rather than surviving a restart to explain it later. What is unexercised is named rather than implied: the scheduler has never run against a real relay console, the interval has never elapsed against a live panel, and no real panel has produced one of these events, so every claim about them is a claim about fixtures.

THE SHIPPED APP NOW CARRIES THE CAPABILITIES ITS OWN INTERFACE OFFERS. The desktop's default feature list was `["ml"]`, so the account subsystem, the NewAPI panel adapter, the browser check-in and the OpenCode provider kinds were all absent from the installed app — while the dashboard offered the account page, the check-in and both OpenCode kinds unconditionally. The panel said "this build contains no account subsystem" to the very people the product was written for, and the panel-backed balance was in the source tree and in no installation of it. **THE REASON THESE WERE KEPT OUT HAS EXPIRED, AND THE REASON IS WORTH KEEPING.** It was "the surface is not reachable yet: nothing probes an account, so with this on the store is constructed and stays empty". The reconciler landed, every declared account is probed and published, and that sentence no longer describes the code. **"OPTIONAL" NOW MEANS WHAT IT SHOULD MEAN: THE CAPABILITY IS IN THE BINARY AND THE BEHAVIOUR IS NOT.** Nothing probes an account until an account is declared; nothing asks a panel until an account exists and the button is pressed; no browser opens until the operator starts a check-in; the OpenCode providers only answer when one is configured. That is the shape ADR-0006 settled on for the learning stack, where `ml_routing.enabled` still defaults to off and an installation that has never promoted a model routes exactly as it did before. `--no-default-features` still builds a desktop app with none of it, so "ship without an account subsystem" remains a build rather than a deletion. The desktop's dependency line on `zroutery-core` still names no features at all, so the core's switches stay independently declared and the activation guard is untouched; `ml` is still first in the default list; and the core's own feature table is unchanged, so the learning build is not perturbed. See E-158.

THE NOTE "ACCOUNT REMAINS OPTIONAL" IS STILL TRUE, AND IT NOW MEANS SOMETHING DIFFERENT FROM WHAT IT USED TO. It used to mean the capability was absent from the shipped app and reachable only by building with a flag, which is a capability no operator meets. It now means the capability is in the binary and the behaviour is not: nothing probes an account until an account is declared, and the desktop's default feature list carries `account`, `newapi` and `account-maint` so the shipped app has the subsystem the account page and the check-in both need. The reconciler that made this possible is the thing the earlier exclusion was waiting for. See E-158.

THE PANEL-BACKED BALANCE IS NOW PROVEN END TO END, AND IT WAS THE ONE BALANCE TEST THAT DID NOT EXIST. Every other balance test drove one piece — the sum of two quotas, the refusal to add two currencies, whether a provider has a balance to ask for at all — and none of them asked a panel. What a user gets when they press *查询余额* on a NewAPI relay is a longer chain: the provider's configuration, the account's own credential resolved through the secret store, an HTTP call to a panel the user cannot see from here, a quota parsed out of the answer and published into a store, read back out, summed, and rendered as a figure in dollars. Every link of that chain was proven on its own, and the chain itself was not proven at all. It is proven now, against a real panel on a real socket that answers the four endpoints the path reads and refuses everything else. **THE FIXTURE IS ARMED AGAINST THE THREE WAYS THIS TEST COULD PASS WHILE THE PRODUCT IS BROKEN**: the provider's own relay key is stored as well, so a path that resolved the provider's credential instead of the account's would meet a relay key where a dashboard token is required, and the adapter refuses to be built with one; the panel records the credentials it was given; and it refuses any credential it was not told to accept. **WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE IS THE REASON THE `NEWAPI` NODE IS STILL PARTIAL**, which is that no *real* panel has ever answered this adapter. A panel on loopback that answers what it is told is still a panel this test wrote. See E-160.
